body: [{"streamId":"01a0bb37-7606-70df-bc8f-02578af4bb01","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskAdded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0bb37-7606-70df-bc8f-02578af4bb01\u0022,\u0022ProjectId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:\u0022A daemon restart that adopts a run in the middle of a verification gate takes over or ends that gate\\u0027s process tree, so the resumed run never crashes on a log file the orphaned tree still holds\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022At startup, when RunSupervisor adopts a run whose recorded phase is a running gate, the daemon either re-attaches to the gate\\u0027s process tree and waits for its result file, or ends that tree and re-runs the gate from the start; it never starts a second gate against a verify-*.log the first still holds open\u0022,\u0022The resumed pipeline treats a locked or unwritable verify log as a retryable infrastructure condition with a bounded retry and a clear log line naming the holder process, never a crash loop every few seconds\u0022,\u0022h9k daemon stop and h9k update --restart print a warning naming any run whose phase is a running gate before stopping, so an operator can wait, and --restart proceeds only with an explicit flag while a gate is live (or waits for it, Brian\\u0027s choice at the walk)\u0022,\u0022Unit tests cover adoption over a running gate on both paths and the locked-log retry; no test creates branches or touches GitHub; no test spawns a real gate\u0022,\u0022dotnet build and dotnet test pass; the decision log carries one entry under this task\\u0027s placeholder\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Captured 2026-09-19 15:5x EDT by the Mac project window from the Windows node window\\u0027s report over the transport. Incident, verbatim in substance: h9k update --restart to v0.10.2 on Windows at 15:44:41 EDT landed two minutes into a56cf16e\\u0027s test gate (the daemon\\u0027s own dotnet test); catch-up adopted the run, but the orphaned test process tree still held verify-test.log locked, and the resumed pipeline crashed on it every 5 seconds until the operator killed the orphan tree by hand at 15:46 EDT; the gate then re-ran from the start under the new daemon. On the Mac the same restart at 15:24 avoided it only because the node window checked the log for a running gate first. Brian\\u0027s rule of the day: only the daemon\\u0027s own in-flight action blocks a restart, live agent sessions are adopted; a running gate IS the daemon\\u0027s own action, and the platform should protect itself rather than rely on an operator reading the log. Pointers: RunSupervisor.AdoptOrphansAsync (adopts on alive-or-result; RunResultFile), VerificationRunner (gate spawn and verify-*.log handling), the daemon stop path in the CLI. Windows-specific note: the lock was a Windows file-share lock; on macOS the same orphan would race the log rather than lock it, so the fix must be cross-platform.
